   294→
   295→```typescript
   296→import * as http from 'node:http'
   297→import * as fs from 'node:fs'
   298→import * as path from 'node:path'
   299→import * as os from 'node:os'
   300→import type { OpenACPCore } from './core.js'
   301→import { createChildLogger } from './log.js'
   302→
   303→const log = createChildLogger({ module: 'api-server' })
   304→
   305→const DEFAULT_PORT_FILE = path.join(os.homedir(), '.openacp', 'api.port')
   306→
   307→export interface ApiConfig {
   308→  port: number
   309→  host: string
   310→}
   311→
   312→export class ApiServer {
   313→  private server: http.Server | null = null
   314→  private actualPort: number = 0
   315→  private portFilePath: string
   316→
   317→  constructor(
   318→    private core: OpenACPCore,
   319→    private config: ApiConfig,
   320→    portFilePath?: string,
   321→  ) {
   322→    this.portFilePath = portFilePath ?? DEFAULT_PORT_FILE
   323→  }
   324→
   325→  async start(): Promise<void> {
   326→    this.server = http.createServer((req, res) => this.handleRequest(req, res))
   327→
   328→    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
   329→      this.server!.on('error', (err: NodeJS.ErrnoException) => {
   330→        if (err.code === 'EADDRINUSE') {
   331→          log.warn({ port: this.config.port }, 'API port in use, continuing without API server')
   332→          this.server = null
   333→          resolve()
   334→        } else {
   335→          reject(err)
   336→        }
   337→      })
   338→
   339→      this.server!.listen(this.config.port, this.config.host, () => {
   340→        const addr = this.server!.address()
   341→        if (addr && typeof addr === 'object') {
   342→          this.actualPort = addr.port
   343→        }
   344→        this.writePortFile()
   345→        log.info({ host: this.config.host, port: this.actualPort }, 'API server listening')
   346→        resolve()
   347→      })
   348→    })
   349→  }
   350→
   351→  async stop(): Promise<void> {
   352→    this.removePortFile()
   353→    if (this.server) {
   354→      await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
   355→        this.server!.close(() => resolve())
   356→      })
   357→      this.server = null
   358→    }
   359→  }
   360→
   361→  getPort(): number {
   362→    return this.actualPort
   363→  }
   364→
   365→  private writePortFile(): void {
   366→    const dir = path.dirname(this.portFilePath)
   367→    fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })
   368→    fs.writeFileSync(this.portFilePath, String(this.actualPort))
   369→  }
   370→
   371→  private removePortFile(): void {
   372→    try {
   373→      fs.unlinkSync(this.portFilePath)
   374→    } catch {
   375→      // ignore if already gone
   376→    }
   377→  }
   378→
   379→  private async handleRequest(req: http.IncomingMessage, res: http.ServerResponse): Promise<void> {
   380→    const method = req.method?.toUpperCase()
   381→    const url = req.url || ''
   382→
   383→    try {
   384→      if (method === 'POST' && url === '/api/sessions') {
   385→        await this.handleCreateSession(req, res)
   386→      } else if (method === 'DELETE' && url.match(/^\/api\/sessions\/(.+)$/)) {
   387→        const sessionId = url.match(/^\/api\/sessions\/(.+)$/)![1]
   388→        await this.handleCancelSession(sessionId, res)
   389→      } else if (method === 'GET' && url === '/api/sessions') {
   390→        await this.handleListSessions(res)
   391→      } else if (method === 'GET' && url === '/api/agents') {
   392→        await this.handleListAgents(res)
   393→      } else {
   394→        this.sendJson(res, 404, { error: 'Not found' })
   395→      }
   396→    } catch (err) {
   397→      log.error({ err }, 'API request error')
   398→      this.sendJson(res, 500, { error: 'Internal server error' })
   399→    }
   400→  }
   401→
   402→  private async handleCreateSession(req: http.IncomingMessage, res: http.ServerResponse): Promise<void> {
   403→    const body = await this.readBody(req)
   404→    let agent: string | undefined
   405→    let workspace: string | undefined
   406→
   407→    if (body) {
   408→      try {
   409→        const parsed = JSON.parse(body)
   410→        agent = parsed.agent
   411→        workspace = parsed.workspace
   412→      } catch {
   413→        this.sendJson(res, 400, { error: 'Invalid JSON body' })
   414→        return
   415→      }
   416→    }
   417→
   418→    const session = await this.core.handleNewSession('api', agent, workspace)
   419→    this.sendJson(res, 200, {
   420→      sessionId: session.id,
   421→      agent: session.agentName,
   422→      status: session.status,
   423→    })
   424→  }
   425→
   426→  private async handleCancelSession(sessionId: string, res: http.ServerResponse): Promise<void> {
   427→    const session = this.core.sessionManager.getSession(sessionId)
   428→    if (!session) {
   429→      this.sendJson(res, 404, { error: `Session "${sessionId}" not found` })
   430→      return
   431→    }
   432→    await session.cancel()
   433→    this.sendJson(res, 200, { ok: true })
   434→  }
   435→
   436→  private async handleListSessions(res: http.ServerResponse): Promise<void> {
   437→    const sessions = this.core.sessionManager.listSessions()
   438→    this.sendJson(res, 200, {
   439→      sessions: sessions.map(s => ({
   440→        id: s.id,
   441→        agent: s.agentName,
   442→        status: s.status,
   443→        name: s.name ?? null,
   444→      })),
   445→    })
   446→  }
   447→
   448→  private async handleListAgents(res: http.ServerResponse): Promise<void> {
   449→    const agents = this.core.agentManager.getAvailableAgents()
   450→    const defaultAgent = this.core.configManager.get().defaultAgent
   451→    this.sendJson(res, 200, {
   452→      agents: agents.map(a => ({
   453→        name: a.name,
   454→        command: a.command,
   455→        args: a.args,
   456→      })),
   457→      default: defaultAgent,
   458→    })
   459→  }
   460→
   461→  private sendJson(res: http.ServerResponse, status: number, data: unknown): void {
   462→    res.writeHead(status, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' })
   463→    res.end(JSON.stringify(data))
   464→  }
   465→
   466→  private readBody(req: http.IncomingMessage): Promise<string> {
   467→    return new Promise((resolve) => {
   468→      let data = ''
   469→      req.on('data', (chunk) => { data += chunk })
   470→      req.on('end', () => resolve(data))
   471→    })
   472→  }
   473→}
   474→```

1→import { ConfigManager } from './config.js'
     2→import { AgentManager } from './agent-manager.js'
     3→import { SessionManager } from './session-manager.js'
     4→import { NotificationManager } from './notification.js'
     5→import { ChannelAdapter } from './channel.js'
     6→import { Session } from './session.js'
     7→import type { IncomingMessage, AgentEvent, OutgoingMessage, PermissionRequest } from './types.js'
     8→import { createChildLogger } from './log.js'
     9→const log = createChildLogger({ module: 'core' })
    10→
    11→export class OpenACPCore {
    12→  configManager: ConfigManager
    13→  agentManager: AgentManager
    14→  sessionManager: SessionManager
    15→  notificationManager: NotificationManager
    16→  adapters: Map<string, ChannelAdapter> = new Map()
    17→
    18→  constructor(configManager: ConfigManager) {
    19→    this.configManager = configManager
    20→    const config = configManager.get()
    21→    this.agentManager = new AgentManager(config)
    22→    this.sessionManager = new SessionManager()
    23→    this.notificationManager = new NotificationManager(this.adapters)
    24→  }
    25→
    26→  registerAdapter(name: string, adapter: ChannelAdapter): void {
    27→    this.adapters.set(name, adapter)
    28→  }
    29→
    30→  async start(): Promise<void> {
    31→    for (const adapter of this.adapters.values()) {
    32→      await adapter.start()
    33→    }
    34→  }
    35→
    36→  async stop(): Promise<void> {
    37→    // 1. Notify users
    38→    try {
    39→      await this.notificationManager.notifyAll({
    40→        sessionId: 'system',
    41→        type: 'error',
    42→        summary: 'OpenACP is shutting down',
    43→      })
    44→    } catch { /* best effort */ }
    45→
    46→    // 2. Destroy all sessions
    47→    await this.sessionManager.destroyAll()
    48→
    49→    // 3. Stop adapters
    50→    for (const adapter of this.adapters.values()) {
    51→      await adapter.stop()
    52→    }
    53→  }
    54→
    55→  // --- Message Routing ---
    56→
    57→  async handleMessage(message: IncomingMessage): Promise<void> {
    58→    const config = this.configManager.get()
    59→    log.debug({ channelId: message.channelId, threadId: message.threadId, userId: message.userId }, 'Incoming message')
    60→
    61→    // Security: check allowed user IDs
    62→    if (config.security.allowedUserIds.length > 0) {
    63→      if (!config.security.allowedUserIds.includes(message.userId)) {
    64→        log.warn({ userId: message.userId }, 'Rejected message from unauthorized user')
    65→        return
    66→      }
    67→    }
    68→
    69→    // Check concurrent session limit
    70→    const activeSessions = this.sessionManager.listSessions()
    71→      .filter(s => s.status === 'active' || s.status === 'initializing')
    72→    if (activeSessions.length >= config.security.maxConcurrentSessions) {
    73→      log.warn({ userId: message.userId, currentCount: activeSessions.length, max: config.security.maxConcurrentSessions }, 'Session limit reached')
    74→      const adapter = this.adapters.get(message.channelId)
    75→      if (adapter) {
    76→        await adapter.sendMessage('system', {
    77→          type: 'error',
    78→          text: `Max concurrent sessions (${config.security.maxConcurrentSessions}) reached. Cancel a session first.`,
    79→        })
    80→      }
    81→      return
    82→    }
    83→
    84→    // Find session by thread
    85→    const session = this.sessionManager.getSessionByThread(message.channelId, message.threadId)
    86→    if (!session) return
    87→
    88→    // Forward to session
    89→    await session.enqueuePrompt(message.text)
    90→  }
    91→
    92→  async handleNewSession(
    93→    channelId: string,
    94→    agentName?: string,
    95→    workspacePath?: string,
    96→  ): Promise<Session> {
    97→    const config = this.configManager.get()
    98→    const resolvedAgent = agentName || config.defaultAgent
    99→    log.info({ channelId, agentName: resolvedAgent }, 'New session request')
   100→    const resolvedWorkspace = this.configManager.resolveWorkspace(
   101→      workspacePath || config.agents[resolvedAgent]?.workingDirectory
   102→    )
   103→
   104→    const session = await this.sessionManager.createSession(
   105→      channelId, resolvedAgent, resolvedWorkspace, this.agentManager
   106→    )
   107→
   108→    // Wire events
   109→    const adapter = this.adapters.get(channelId)
   110→    if (adapter) {
   111→      this.wireSessionEvents(session, adapter)
   112→    }
   113→
   114→    return session
   115→  }
   116→
   117→  async handleNewChat(
   118→    channelId: string,
   119→    currentThreadId: string,
   120→  ): Promise<Session | null> {
   121→    const currentSession = this.sessionManager.getSessionByThread(channelId, currentThreadId)
   122→    if (!currentSession) return null
   123→
   124→    return this.handleNewSession(
   125→      channelId,
   126→      currentSession.agentName,
   127→      currentSession.workingDirectory,
   128→    )
   129→  }
   130→
   131→  // --- Event Wiring ---
   132→
   133→  private toOutgoingMessage(event: AgentEvent): OutgoingMessage {
   134→    switch (event.type) {
   135→      case 'text':
   136→        return { type: 'text', text: event.content }
   137→      case 'thought':
   138→        return { type: 'thought', text: event.content }
   139→      case 'tool_call':
   140→        return { type: 'tool_call', text: event.name, metadata: { id: event.id, kind: event.kind, status: event.status, content: event.content, locations: event.locations } }
   141→      case 'tool_update':
   142→        return { type: 'tool_update', text: '', metadata: { id: event.id, status: event.status, content: event.content } }
   143→      case 'plan':
   144→        return { type: 'plan', text: '', metadata: { entries: event.entries } }
   145→      case 'usage':
   146→        return { type: 'usage', text: '', metadata: { tokensUsed: event.tokensUsed, contextSize: event.contextSize, cost: event.cost } }
   147→      default:
   148→        return { type: 'text', text: '' }
   149→    }
   150→  }
   151→
   152→  // Public — adapters call this for assistant session wiring
   153→  wireSessionEvents(session: Session, adapter: ChannelAdapter): void {
   154→    // Set adapter reference for autoName → renameSessionThread
   155→    session.adapter = adapter
   156→
   157→    session.agentInstance.onSessionUpdate = (event: AgentEvent) => {
   158→      switch (event.type) {
   159→        case 'text':
   160→        case 'thought':
   161→        case 'tool_call':
   162→        case 'tool_update':
   163→        case 'plan':
   164→        case 'usage':
   165→          adapter.sendMessage(session.id, this.toOutgoingMessage(event))
   166→          break
   167→
   168→        case 'session_end':
   169→          session.status = 'finished'
   170→          adapter.cleanupSkillCommands(session.id)
   171→          adapter.sendMessage(session.id, { type: 'session_end', text: `Done (${event.reason})` })
   172→          this.notificationManager.notify(session.channelId, {
   173→            sessionId: session.id,
   174→            sessionName: session.name,
   175→            type: 'completed',
   176→            summary: `Session "${session.name || session.id}" completed`,
   177→          })
   178→          break
   179→
   180→        case 'error':
   181→          adapter.cleanupSkillCommands(session.id)
   182→          adapter.sendMessage(session.id, { type: 'error', text: event.message })
   183→          this.notificationManager.notify(session.channelId, {
   184→            sessionId: session.id,
   185→            sessionName: session.name,
   186→            type: 'error',
   187→            summary: event.message,
   188→          })
   189→          break
   190→
   191→        case 'commands_update':
   192→          log.debug({ commands: event.commands }, 'Commands available')
   193→          adapter.sendSkillCommands(session.id, event.commands)
   194→          break
   195→      }
   196→    }
   197→
   198→    session.agentInstance.onPermissionRequest = async (request: PermissionRequest) => {
   199→      // Set pending BEFORE sending UI to avoid race condition
   200→      const promise = new Promise<string>((resolve) => {
   201→        session.pendingPermission = { requestId: request.id, resolve }
   202→      })
   203→
   204→      // Send permission UI to session topic (notification is sent by adapter)
   205→      await adapter.sendPermissionRequest(session.id, request)
   206→
   207→      // Wait for user response — adapter resolves this promise
   208→      return promise
   209→    }
   210→  }
   211→}
   212→

1→#!/usr/bin/env node
     2→
     3→import { ConfigManager } from './core/config.js'
     4→import { OpenACPCore } from './core/core.js'
     5→import { loadAdapterFactory } from './core/plugin-manager.js'
     6→import { initLogger, shutdownLogger, cleanupOldSessionLogs, log } from './core/log.js'
     7→import { TelegramAdapter } from './adapters/telegram/index.js'
     8→
     9→let shuttingDown = false
    10→
    11→export async function startServer() {
    12→  // 1. Check config exists, run setup if not
    13→  const configManager = new ConfigManager()
    14→  const configExists = await configManager.exists()
    15→
    16→  if (!configExists) {
    17→    const { runSetup } = await import('./core/setup.js')
    18→    const shouldStart = await runSetup(configManager)
    19→    if (!shouldStart) process.exit(0)
    20→  }
    21→
    22→  // 2. Load config (validates with Zod)
    23→  await configManager.load()
    24→  const config = configManager.get()
    25→  initLogger(config.logging)
    26→  log.info({ configPath: configManager.getConfigPath() }, 'Config loaded')
    27→
    28→  // Async cleanup of old session logs (non-blocking)
    29→  cleanupOldSessionLogs(config.logging.sessionLogRetentionDays).catch(err =>
    30→    log.warn({ err }, 'Session log cleanup failed')
    31→  )
    32→
    33→  // 3. Create core
    34→  const core = new OpenACPCore(configManager)
    35→
    36→  // 4. Register adapters from config
    37→  for (const [channelName, channelConfig] of Object.entries(config.channels)) {
    38→    if (!channelConfig.enabled) continue
    39→
    40→    if (channelName === 'telegram') {
    41→      core.registerAdapter('telegram', new TelegramAdapter(core, channelConfig as any))
    42→      log.info({ adapter: 'telegram' }, 'Adapter registered')
    43→    } else if (channelConfig.adapter) {
    44→      // Plugin adapter
    45→      const factory = await loadAdapterFactory(channelConfig.adapter)
    46→      if (factory) {
    47→        const adapter = factory.createAdapter(core, channelConfig)
    48→        core.registerAdapter(channelName, adapter)
    49→        log.info({ adapter: channelName, plugin: channelConfig.adapter }, 'Adapter registered')
    50→      } else {
    51→        const name = channelName
    52→        const err = channelConfig.adapter
    53→        log.error({ adapter: name, err }, 'Failed to load adapter')
    54→      }
    55→    } else {
    56→      log.error({ adapter: channelName }, 'Channel has no built-in adapter; set "adapter" field to a plugin package')
    57→    }
    58→  }
    59→
    60→  if (core.adapters.size === 0) {
    61→    log.error('No channels enabled. Enable at least one channel in config.')
    62→    process.exit(1)
    63→  }
    64→
    65→  // 5. Start
    66→  await core.start()
    67→
    68→  // 6. Log ready
    69→  const agents = Object.keys(config.agents)
    70→  log.info({ agents }, 'OpenACP started')
    71→  log.info('Press Ctrl+C to stop')
    72→
    73→  // 7. Graceful shutdown
    74→  const shutdown = async (signal: string) => {
    75→    if (shuttingDown) return
    76→    shuttingDown = true
    77→    log.info({ signal }, 'Signal received, shutting down')
    78→
    79→    try {
    80→      await core.stop()
    81→    } catch (err) {
    82→      log.error({ err }, 'Error during shutdown')
    83→    }
    84→
    85→    // Clean up PID file if running as daemon
    86→    if (process.argv.includes('--daemon-child')) {
    87→      const { removePidFile, getPidPath } = await import('./core/daemon.js')
    88→      removePidFile(getPidPath())
    89→    }
    90→
    91→    await shutdownLogger()
    92→    process.exit(0)
    93→  }
    94→
    95→  process.on('SIGINT', () => shutdown('SIGINT'))
    96→  process.on('SIGTERM', () => shutdown('SIGTERM'))
    97→
    98→  process.on('uncaughtException', (err) => {
    99→    log.error({ err }, 'Uncaught exception')
   100→  })
   101→
   102→  process.on('unhandledRejection', (err) => {
   103→    log.error({ err }, 'Unhandled rejection')
   104→  })
   105→}
   106→
   107→// Direct execution for dev (node dist/main.js)
   108→const isDirectExecution = process.argv[1]?.endsWith('main.js')
   109→if (isDirectExecution) {
   110→  startServer().catch((err) => {
   111→    log.error({ err }, 'Fatal error')
   112→    process.exit(1)
   113→  })

Now I have a thorough picture of both documents and the codebase. Let me compile my review.

---

# Plan Review: `2026-03-20-runtime-api-cli.md`

## Overall Assessment: Issues Found

The plan is well-structured and covers most of the spec, but there are several issues ranging from Critical to Minor.

---

## 1. Spec Compliance

### Critical: `listSessions()` vs `listAllSessions()` — Spec Requires a New Method, Plan Skips It

The spec (Section 2, "Core Access Pattern") explicitly calls out:

> **List sessions**: `core.sessionManager.listAllSessions()` — new method needed (existing `listSessions(channelId)` filters by channel; we need all sessions)

Looking at the actual `SessionManager` in `/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/OpenACP/src/core/session-manager.ts` (line 37–41):

```typescript
listSessions(channelId?: string): Session[] {
  const all = Array.from(this.sessions.values())
  if (channelId) return all.filter(s => s.channelId === channelId)
  return all
}
```

The context block at the top of Task 2 in the plan states correctly:

> `core.sessionManager.listSessions()` (no args) returns all sessions across all channels

This is technically true — passing no argument already returns all sessions. However, the spec explicitly required adding a new `listAllSessions()` method. The plan sidesteps this by calling `listSessions()` with no args and documenting that as the approach. The plan contradicts its own context vs. the spec without explaining the deviation. An engineer following the plan will not add the method; an engineer following the spec will expect it.

**Recommendation:** The plan must either (a) add a Task step to add `listAllSessions()` as a semantic alias for `listSessions()` in `SessionManager`, or (b) explicitly document that this spec requirement is intentionally skipped because the existing method already covers it. Silently omitting it is a source of confusion.

---

### Important: 429 Error Response is Missing from the Implementation

The spec (Section 2, "Error Responses") lists:

| Status | Condition |
|--------|-----------|
| 429 | Max concurrent sessions reached |

The plan's `handleCreateSession` implementation in `api-server.ts` does not check or enforce the max concurrent sessions limit.    296→import * as http from 'node:http'
   297→import * as fs from 'node:fs'
   298→import * as path from 'node:path'
   299→import * as os from 'node:os'
   300→import type { OpenACPCore } from './core.js'
   301→import { createChildLogger } from './log.js'
   302→
   303→const log = createChildLogger({ module: 'api-server' })
   304→
   305→const DEFAULT_PORT_FILE = path.join(os.homedir(), '.openacp', 'api.port')
   306→
   307→export interface ApiConfig {
   308→  port: number
   309→  host: string
   310→}
   311→
   312→export class ApiServer {
   313→  private server: http.Server | null = null
   314→  private actualPort: number = 0
   315→  private portFilePath: string
   316→
   317→  constructor(
   318→    private core: OpenACPCore,
   319→    private config: ApiConfig,
   320→    portFilePath?: string,
   321→  ) {
   322→    this.portFilePath = portFilePath ?? DEFAULT_PORT_FILE
   323→  }
   324→
   325→  async start(): Promise<void> {
   326→    this.server = http.createServer((req, res) => this.handleRequest(req, res))
   327→
   328→    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
   329→      this.server!.on('error', (err: NodeJS.ErrnoException) => {
   330→        if (err.code === 'EADDRINUSE') {
   331→          log.warn({ port: this.config.port }, 'API port in use, continuing without API server')
   332→          this.server = null
   333→          resolve()
   334→        } else {
   335→          reject(err)
   336→        }
   337→      })
   338→
   339→      this.server!.listen(this.config.port, this.config.host, () => {
   340→        const addr = this.server!.address()
   341→        if (addr && typeof addr === 'object') {
   342→          this.actualPort = addr.port
   343→        }
   344→        this.writePortFile()
   345→        log.info({ host: this.config.host, port: this.actualPort }, 'API server listening')
   346→        resolve()
   347→      })
   348→    })
   349→  }
   350→
   351→  async stop(): Promise<void> {
   352→    this.removePortFile()
   353→    if (this.server) {
   354→      await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
   355→        this.server!.close(() => resolve())
   356→      })
   357→      this.server = null
   358→    }
   359→  }
   360→
   361→  getPort(): number {
   362→    return this.actualPort
   363→  }
   364→
   365→  private writePortFile(): void {
   366→    const dir = path.dirname(this.portFilePath)
   367→    fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })
   368→    fs.writeFileSync(this.portFilePath, String(this.actualPort))
   369→  }
   370→
   371→  private removePortFile(): void {
   372→    try {
   373→      fs.unlinkSync(this.portFilePath)
   374→    } catch {
   375→      // ignore if already gone
   376→    }
   377→  }
   378→
   379→  private async handleRequest(req: http.IncomingMessage, res: http.ServerResponse): Promise<void> {
   380→    const method = req.method?.toUpperCase()
   381→    const url = req.url || ''
   382→
   383→    try {
   384→      if (method === 'POST' && url === '/api/sessions') {
   385→        await this.handleCreateSession(req, res)
   386→      } else if (method === 'DELETE' && url.match(/^\/api\/sessions\/(.+)$/)) {
   387→        const sessionId = url.match(/^\/api\/sessions\/(.+)$/)![1]
   388→        await this.handleCancelSession(sessionId, res)
   389→      } else if (method === 'GET' && url === '/api/sessions') {
   390→        await this.handleListSessions(res)
   391→      } else if (method === 'GET' && url === '/api/agents') {
   392→        await this.handleListAgents(res)
   393→      } else {
   394→        this.sendJson(res, 404, { error: 'Not found' })
   395→      }
   396→    } catch (err) {
   397→      log.error({ err }, 'API request error')
   398→      this.sendJson(res, 500, { error: 'Internal server error' })
   399→    }
   400→  }
   401→
   402→  private async handleCreateSession(req: http.IncomingMessage, res: http.ServerResponse): Promise<void> {
   403→    const body = await this.readBody(req)
   404→    let agent: string | undefined
   405→    let workspace: string | undefined
   406→
   407→    if (body) {
   408→      try {
   409→        const parsed = JSON.parse(body)
   410→        agent = parsed.agent
   411→        workspace = parsed.workspace
   412→      } catch {
   413→        this.sendJson(res, 400, { error: 'Invalid JSON body' })
   414→        return
   415→      }
   416→    }
   417→
   418→    const session = await this.core.handleNewSession('api', agent, workspace)
   419→    this.sendJson(res, 200, {
   420→      sessionId: session.id,
   421→      agent: session.agentName,
   422→      status: session.status,
   423→    })
   424→  }
   425→
   426→  private async handleCancelSession(sessionId: string, res: http.ServerResponse): Promise<void> {
   427→    const session = this.core.sessionManager.getSession(sessionId)
   428→    if (!session) {
   429→      this.sendJson(res, 404, { error: `Session "${sessionId}" not found` })
   430→      return
   431→    }
   432→    await session.cancel()
   433→    this.sendJson(res, 200, { ok: true })
   434→  }
   435→
   436→  private async handleListSessions(res: http.ServerResponse): Promise<void> {
   437→    const sessions = this.core.sessionManager.listSessions()
   438→    this.sendJson(res, 200, {
   439→      sessions: sessions.map(s => ({
   440→        id: s.id,
   441→        agent: s.agentName,
   442→        status: s.status,
   443→        name: s.name ?? null,
   444→      })),
   445→    })
   446→  }
   447→
   448→  private async handleListAgents(res: http.ServerResponse): Promise<void> {
   449→    const agents = this.core.agentManager.getAvailableAgents()
   450→    const defaultAgent = this.core.configManager.get().defaultAgent
   451→    this.sendJson(res, 200, {
   452→      agents: agents.map(a => ({
   453→        name: a.name,
   454→        command: a.command,
   455→        args: a.args,
   456→      })),
   457→      default: defaultAgent,
   458→    })
   459→  }
   460→
   461→  private sendJson(res: http.ServerResponse, status: number, data: unknown): void {
   462→    res.writeHead(status, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' })
   463→    res.end(JSON.stringify(data))
   464→  }
   465→
   466→  private readBody(req: http.IncomingMessage): Promise<string> {
   467→    return new Promise((resolve) => {
   468→      let data = ''
   469→      req.on('data', (chunk) => { data += chunk })
   470→      req.on('end', () => resolve(data))
   471→    })
   472→  }
   473→}
   474→```

# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching fresh subagent per task, with two-stage review after each: spec compliance review first, then code quality review.

**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review (spec then quality) = high quality, fast iteration

## When to Use

```dot

    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];

    "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];

    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Two-stage review after each task: spec compliance first, then code quality
- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)

    "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?";
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" -> "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="re-review"];
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="yes"];
    "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?";
    "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" -> "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" -> "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="re-review"];
    "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" -> "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" [label="yes"];
    "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" -> "More tasks remain?";
    "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [label="yes"];
    "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" [label="no"];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" -> "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch";
}
```

## Model Selection

Use the least powerful model that can handle each role to conserve cost and increase speed.

**Mechanical implementation tasks** (isolated functions, clear specs, 1-2 files): use a fast, cheap model. Most implementation tasks are mechanical when the plan is well-specified.

**Integration and judgment tasks** (multi-file coordination, pattern matching, debugging): use a standard model.

**Architecture, design, and review tasks**: use the most capable available model.

**Task complexity signals:**
- Touches 1-2 files with a complete spec → cheap model
- Touches multiple files with integration concerns → standard model
- Requires design judgment or broad codebase understanding → most capable model

## Handling Implementer Status

Implementer subagents report one of four statuses. Handle each appropriately:

**DONE:** Proceed to spec compliance review.

**DONE_WITH_CONCERNS:** The implementer completed the work but flagged doubts. Read the concerns before proceeding. If the concerns are about correctness or scope, address them before review. If they're observations (e.g., "this file is getting large"), note them and proceed to review.

**NEEDS_CONTEXT:** The implementer needs information that wasn't provided. Provide the missing context and re-dispatch.

**BLOCKED:** The implementer cannot complete the task. Assess the blocker:
1. If it's a context problem, provide more context and re-dispatch with the same model
2. If the task requires more reasoning, re-dispatch with a more capable model
3. If the task is too large, break it into smaller pieces
4. If the plan itself is wrong, escalate to the human

**Never** ignore an escalation or force the same model to retry without changes. If the implementer said it's stuck, something needs to change.

## Prompt Templates

- `./implementer-prompt.md` - Dispatch implementer subagent
- `./spec-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch spec compliance reviewer subagent
- `./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent

## Example Workflow

```

[Extract all 5 tasks with full text and context]
[Create TodoWrite with all tasks]

You: "User level (~/.config/superpowers/hooks/)"

Implementer: "Got it. Implementing now..."
[Later] Implementer:
  - Implemented install-hook command
  - Added tests, 5/5 passing
  - Self-review: Found I missed --force flag, added it
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]

[Get git SHAs, dispatch code quality reviewer]

[Mark Task 1 complete]

Task 2: Recovery modes

[Get Task 2 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: [No questions, proceeds]

  - Added verify/repair modes
  - 8/8 tests passing
  - Self-review: All good
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]

  - Missing: Progress reporting (spec says "report every 100 items")
  - Extra: Added --json flag (not requested)

[Implementer fixes issues]

[Spec reviewer reviews again]

[Dispatch code quality reviewer]

...

[After all tasks]

Done!
```

## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - REQUIRED: Set up isolated workspace before starting
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:requesting-code-review** - Code review template for reviewer subagents
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

**Subagents should use:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - Subagents follow TDD for each task

**Alternative workflow:**
- **superpowers:executing-plans** - Use for parallel session instead of same-session execution

# Implementer Subagent Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching an implementer subagent.

```
Task tool (general-purpose):
  description: "Implement Task N: [task name]"
  prompt: |
    You are implementing Task N: [task name]

    ## Task Description

    [FULL TEXT of task from plan - paste it here, don't make subagent read file]

    ## Context

    [Scene-setting: where this fits, dependencies, architectural context]

    ## Before You Begin

    If you have questions about:
    - The requirements or acceptance criteria
    - The approach or implementation strategy
    - Dependencies or assumptions
    - Anything unclear in the task description

    **Ask them now.** Raise any concerns before starting work.

    ## Your Job

    Once you're clear on requirements:
    1. Implement exactly what the task specifies
    2. Write tests (following TDD if task says to)
    3. Verify implementation works
    4. Commit your work
    5. Self-review (see below)
    6. Report back

    Work from: [directory]

    **While you work:** If you encounter something unexpected or unclear, **ask questions**.
    It's always OK to pause and clarify. Don't guess or make assumptions.

    ## Code Organization

    You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more
    reliable when files are focused. Keep this in mind:
    - Follow the file structure defined in the plan
    - Each file should have one clear responsibility with a well-defined interface
    - If a file you're creating is growing beyond the plan's intent, stop and report
      it as DONE_WITH_CONCERNS — don't split files on your own without plan guidance
    - If an existing file you're modifying is already large or tangled, work carefully
      and note it as a concern in your report
    - In existing codebases, follow established patterns. Improve code you're touching
      the way a good developer would, but don't restructure things outside your task.

    ## When You're in Over Your Head

    It is always OK to stop and say "this is too hard for me." Bad work is worse than
    no work. You will not be penalized for escalating.

    **STOP and escalate when:**
    - The task requires architectural decisions with multiple valid approaches
    - You need to understand code beyond what was provided and can't find clarity
    - You feel uncertain about whether your approach is correct
    - The task involves restructuring existing code in ways the plan didn't anticipate
    - You've been reading file after file trying to understand the system without progress

    **How to escalate:** Report back with status BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT. Describe
    specifically what you're stuck on, what you've tried, and what kind of help you need.
    The controller can provide more context, re-dispatch with a more capable model,
    or break the task into smaller pieces.

    ## Before Reporting Back: Self-Review

    Review your work with fresh eyes. Ask yourself:

    **Completeness:**
    - Did I fully implement everything in the spec?
    - Did I miss any requirements?
    - Are there edge cases I didn't handle?

    **Quality:**
    - Is this my best work?
    - Are names clear and accurate (match what things do, not how they work)?
    - Is the code clean and maintainable?

    **Discipline:**
    - Did I avoid overbuilding (YAGNI)?
    - Did I only build what was requested?
    - Did I follow existing patterns in the codebase?

    **Testing:**
    - Do tests actually verify behavior (not just mock behavior)?
    - Did I follow TDD if required?
    - Are tests comprehensive?

    If you find issues during self-review, fix them now before reporting.

    ## Report Format

    When done, report:
    - **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT
    - What you implemented (or what you attempted, if blocked)
    - What you tested and test results
    - Files changed
    - Self-review findings (if any)
    - Any issues or concerns

    Use DONE_WITH_CONCERNS if you completed the work but have doubts about correctness.
    Use BLOCKED if you cannot complete the task. Use NEEDS_CONTEXT if you need
    information that wasn't provided. Never silently produce work you're unsure about.
```

     6→import { Session } from './session.js'
     7→import type { IncomingMessage, AgentEvent, OutgoingMessage, PermissionRequest } from './types.js'
     8→import { createChildLogger } from './log.js'
     9→const log = createChildLogger({ module: 'core' })
    10→
    11→export class OpenACPCore {
    12→  configManager: ConfigManager
    13→  agentManager: AgentManager
    14→  sessionManager: SessionManager
    15→  notificationManager: NotificationManager
    16→  adapters: Map<string, ChannelAdapter> = new Map()
    17→
    18→  constructor(configManager: ConfigManager) {
    19→    this.configManager = configManager
    20→    const config = configManager.get()
    21→    this.agentManager = new AgentManager(config)
    22→    this.sessionManager = new SessionManager()
    23→    this.notificationManager = new NotificationManager(this.adapters)
    24→  }
    25→
    26→  registerAdapter(name: string, adapter: ChannelAdapter): void {
    27→    this.adapters.set(name, adapter)
    28→  }
    29→
    30→  async start(): Promise<void> {
    31→    for (const adapter of this.adapters.values()) {
    32→      await adapter.start()
    33→    }
    34→  }
    35→
    36→  async stop(): Promise<void> {
    37→    // 1. Notify users
    38→    try {
    39→      await this.notificationManager.notifyAll({
    40→        sessionId: 'system',
    41→        type: 'error',
    42→        summary: 'OpenACP is shutting down',
    43→      })
    44→    } catch { /* best effort */ }
    45→
    46→    // 2. Destroy all sessions
    47→    await this.sessionManager.destroyAll()
    48→
    49→    // 3. Stop adapters
    50→    for (const adapter of this.adapters.values()) {
    51→      await adapter.stop()
    52→    }
    53→  }
    54→
    55→  // --- Message Routing ---
    56→
    57→  async handleMessage(message: IncomingMessage): Promise<void> {
    58→    const config = this.configManager.get()
    59→    log.debug({ channelId: message.channelId, threadId: message.threadId, userId: message.userId }, 'Incoming message')
    60→
    61→    // Security: check allowed user IDs
    62→    if (config.security.allowedUserIds.length > 0) {
    63→      if (!config.security.allowedUserIds.includes(message.userId)) {
    64→        log.warn({ userId: message.userId }, 'Rejected message from unauthorized user')
    65→        return
    66→      }
    67→    }
    68→
    69→    // Check concurrent session limit
    70→    const activeSessions = this.sessionManager.listSessions()
    71→      .filter(s => s.status === 'active' || s.status === 'initializing')
    72→    if (activeSessions.length >= config.security.maxConcurrentSessions) {
    73→      log.warn({ userId: message.userId, currentCount: activeSessions.length, max: config.security.maxConcurrentSessions }, 'Session limit reached')
    74→      const adapter = this.adapters.get(message.channelId)
    75→      if (adapter) {
    76→        await adapter.sendMessage('system', {
    77→          type: 'error',
    78→          text: `Max concurrent sessions (${config.security.maxConcurrentSessions}) reached. Cancel a session first.`,
    79→        })
    80→      }
    81→      return
    82→    }
    83→
    84→    // Find session by thread
    85→    const session = this.sessionManager.getSessionByThread(message.channelId, message.threadId)
    86→    if (!session) return

    88→    // Forward to session
    89→    await session.enqueuePrompt(message.text)

    99→    log.info({ channelId, agentName: resolvedAgent }, 'New session request')

   102→    )
   103→

   106→    )

   116→
   117→  async handleNewChat(
   118→    channelId: string,
   119→    currentThreadId: string,

   126→      currentSession.agentName,
   127→      currentSession.workingDirectory,
   128→    )

   131→  // --- Event Wiring ---
   132→
   133→  private toOutgoingMessage(event: AgentEvent): OutgoingMessage {
   134→    switch (event.type) {
   135→      case 'text':
   136→        return { type: 'text', text: event.content }
   137→      case 'thought':
   138→        return { type: 'thought', text: event.content }
   139→      case 'tool_call':

   141→      case 'tool_update':
   142→        return { type: 'tool_update', text: '', metadata: { id: event.id, status: event.status, content: event.content } }
   143→      case 'plan':
   144→        return { type: 'plan', text: '', metadata: { entries: event.entries } }
   145→      case 'usage':

   132→    const cm = new ConfigManager()

   134→    if (await cm.exists()) {

   138→    const logFile = pathMod.join(expandHome(logDir), 'openacp.log')
   139→    const tail = spawn('tail', ['-f', '-n', '50', logFile], { stdio: 'inherit' })
   140→    tail.on('error', (err: Error) => {

   148→    const { runConfigEditor } = await import('./core/config-editor.js')
   149→    const { ConfigManager } = await import('./core/config.js')
   150→    const cm = new ConfigManager()
   151→    if (!(await cm.exists())) {

   178→  const cm = new ConfigManager()
   179→
   180→  // If no config, run setup first

   182→    const { runSetup } = await import('./core/setup.js')
   183→    const shouldStart = await runSetup(cm)
   184→    if (!shouldStart) process.exit(0)

   188→  await cm.load()
   189→  const config = cm.get()
   190→
   191→  if (!forceForeground && config.runMode === 'daemon') {
   192→    // Daemon mode: spawn background process
   193→    const { startDaemon, getPidPath } = await import('./core/daemon.js')
   194→    const result = startDaemon(getPidPath(), config.logging.logDir)

   196→      console.error(result.error)
   197→      process.exit(1)
   198→    }

   205→  clearUserStopped()

   207→  await startServer()
   208→}

     5→import { loadAdapterFactory } from './core/plugin-manager.js'
     6→import { initLogger, shutdownLogger, cleanupOldSessionLogs, log } from './core/log.js'
     7→import { TelegramAdapter } from './adapters/telegram/index.js'
     8→
     9→let shuttingDown = false
    10→
    11→export async function startServer() {
    12→  // 0. If running as daemon child, check state and write PID file
    13→  if (process.argv.includes('--daemon-child')) {
    14→    const { writePidFile, readPidFile, getPidPath, isUserStopped } = await import('./core/daemon.js')
    15→
    16→    // If user explicitly stopped the daemon, don't auto-start on boot
    17→    if (isUserStopped()) {
    18→      process.exit(0)
    19→    }
    20→
    21→    const pidPath = getPidPath()
    22→    const existingPid = readPidFile(pidPath)
    23→    if (existingPid !== null && existingPid !== process.pid) {
    24→      try {
    25→        process.kill(existingPid, 0)
    26→        console.error(`Another OpenACP instance is already running (PID ${existingPid}). Exiting.`)
    27→        process.exit(1)
    28→      } catch {
    29→        // Stale PID file — safe to overwrite
    30→      }
    31→    }
    32→    writePidFile(pidPath, process.pid)
    33→  }
    34→
    35→  // 1. Check config exists, run setup if not
    36→  const configManager = new ConfigManager()
    37→  const configExists = await configManager.exists()
    38→
    39→  if (!configExists) {
    40→    const { runSetup } = await import('./core/setup.js')
    41→    const shouldStart = await runSetup(configManager)
    42→    if (!shouldStart) process.exit(0)
    43→  }
    44→
    45→  // 2. Load config (validates with Zod)
    46→  await configManager.load()
    47→  const config = configManager.get()
    48→  initLogger(config.logging)
    49→  log.info({ configPath: configManager.getConfigPath() }, 'Config loaded')
    50→
    51→  // Async cleanup of old session logs (non-blocking)
    52→  cleanupOldSessionLogs(config.logging.sessionLogRetentionDays).catch(err =>
    53→    log.warn({ err }, 'Session log cleanup failed')
    54→  )
    55→
    56→  // 3. Create core
    57→  const core = new OpenACPCore(configManager)
    58→
    59→  // 4. Register adapters from config
    60→  for (const [channelName, channelConfig] of Object.entries(config.channels)) {
    61→    if (!channelConfig.enabled) continue
    62→
    63→    if (channelName === 'telegram') {
    64→      core.registerAdapter('telegram', new TelegramAdapter(core, channelConfig as any))
    65→      log.info({ adapter: 'telegram' }, 'Adapter registered')
    66→    } else if (channelConfig.adapter) {
    67→      // Plugin adapter
    68→      const factory = await loadAdapterFactory(channelConfig.adapter)
    69→      if (factory) {
    70→        const adapter = factory.createAdapter(core, channelConfig)
    71→        core.registerAdapter(channelName, adapter)
    72→        log.info({ adapter: channelName, plugin: channelConfig.adapter }, 'Adapter registered')
    73→      } else {
    74→        const name = channelName
    75→        const err = channelConfig.adapter
    76→        log.error({ adapter: name, err }, 'Failed to load adapter')
    77→      }
    78→    } else {
    79→      log.error({ adapter: channelName }, 'Channel has no built-in adapter; set "adapter" field to a plugin package')
    80→    }
    81→  }
    82→
    83→  if (core.adapters.size === 0) {
    84→    log.error('No channels enabled. Enable at least one channel in config.')
    85→    process.exit(1)
    86→  }
    87→
    88→  // 5. Start
    89→  await core.start()
    90→
    91→  // 6. Log ready
    92→  const agents = Object.keys(config.agents)
    93→  log.info({ agents }, 'OpenACP started')
    94→  log.info('Press Ctrl+C to stop')
    95→
    96→  // 7. Graceful shutdown
    97→  const shutdown = async (signal: string) => {
    98→    if (shuttingDown) return
    99→    shuttingDown = true
   100→    log.info({ signal }, 'Signal received, shutting down')
   101→
   102→    try {
   103→      await core.stop()
   104→    } catch (err) {
   105→      log.error({ err }, 'Error during shutdown')
   106→    }
   107→
   108→    // Clean up PID file if running as daemon
   109→    if (process.argv.includes('--daemon-child')) {
   110→      const { removePidFile, getPidPath } = await import('./core/daemon.js')
   111→      removePidFile(getPidPath())
   112→    }
   113→
   114→    await shutdownLogger()
   115→    process.exit(0)
   116→  }
   117→
   118→  process.on('SIGINT', () => shutdown('SIGINT'))
   119→  process.on('SIGTERM', () => shutdown('SIGTERM'))
   120→
   121→  process.on('uncaughtException', (err) => {
   122→    log.error({ err }, 'Uncaught exception')
   123→  })
   124→
   125→  process.on('unhandledRejection', (err) => {
   126→    log.error({ err }, 'Unhandled rejection')
   127→  })
   128→}
   129→
   130→// Direct execution for dev (node dist/main.js)
   131→const isDirectExecution = process.argv[1]?.endsWith('main.js')
   132→if (isDirectExecution) {
   133→  startServer().catch((err) => {
   134→    log.error({ err }, 'Fatal error')
   135→    process.exit(1)
   136→  })

    54→    log.warn({ err }, 'Session log cleanup failed')

// --- Edit: API ---

async function editApi(config: Config, updates: ConfigUpdates): Promise<void> {
  const api = config.api ?? { port: 21420, host: '127.0.0.1' }

  console.log(ok(`API port set to ${newPort.trim()}`))
}

    25→      try {

    27→        console.error(`Another OpenACP instance is already running (PID ${existingPid}). Exiting.`)
    28→        process.exit(1)

    34→  }

    38→  const configExists = await configManager.exists()

    42→    const shouldStart = await runSetup(configManager)
    43→    if (!shouldStart) process.exit(0)
    44→  }
    45→
    46→  // 2. Load config (validates with Zod)
    47→  await configManager.load()
    48→  const config = configManager.get()
    49→  initLogger(config.logging)
    50→  log.info({ configPath: configManager.getConfigPath() }, 'Config loaded')
    51→
    52→  // Async cleanup of old session logs (non-blocking)
    53→  cleanupOldSessionLogs(config.logging.sessionLogRetentionDays).catch(err =>
    54→    log.warn({ err }, 'Session log cleanup failed')
    55→  )

    57→  // 3. Create core

    61→  for (const [channelName, channelConfig] of Object.entries(config.channels)) {
    62→    if (!channelConfig.enabled) continue
    63→
    64→    if (channelName === 'telegram') {
    65→      core.registerAdapter('telegram', new TelegramAdapter(core, channelConfig as any))
    66→      log.info({ adapter: 'telegram' }, 'Adapter registered')
    67→    } else if (channelConfig.adapter) {

    70→      if (factory) {

    72→        core.registerAdapter(channelName, adapter)

    74→      } else {

    78→      }
    79→    } else {

    81→    }
    82→  }

    95→    log.info({ signal }, 'Signal received, shutting down')

    99→      await core.stop()

   111→    process.exit(0)

   119→  })
   120→

   123→  })

   128→  await apiServer.start()

   132→  log.info({ agents }, 'OpenACP started')
   133→  log.info('Press Ctrl+C to stop')
   134→}

## Task Description

Modify `src/main.ts` to start and stop the ApiServer alongside the daemon.

**Important scoping rule:** The `apiServer` variable must be declared with `let` BEFORE the `shutdown` closure is defined, then assigned after `core.start()`. This avoids temporal dead zone issues.

## Steps

1. Read `src/main.ts` first.

2. Add import after existing imports:
```typescript
import { ApiServer } from './core/api-server.js'
```

3. Inside `startServer()`, declare `let apiServer: ApiServer | undefined` BEFORE the `shutdown` function definition (before `const shutdown = async...`).

4. After `await core.start()` (and after the `let apiServer` declaration), add:
```typescript
  apiServer = new ApiServer(core, config.api)
  await apiServer.start()
```

5. In the `shutdown` function, add BEFORE `await core.stop()`:
```typescript
      if (apiServer) await apiServer.stop()
```

6. Run: `pnpm test && pnpm build`

7. Commit:
```bash
git add src/main.ts
git commit -m "feat(main): integrate API server into daemon lifecycle"
```

The ApiServer class is at `src/core/api-server.ts` (created in Task 2). The config now has `config.api` with `{ port: number, host: string }` (from Task 1). The ApiServer manages its own port file and handles EADDRINUSE gracefully.

// --- Edit: API ---

async function editApi(config: Config, updates: ConfigUpdates): Promise<void> {
  const api = config.api ?? { port: 21420, host: '127.0.0.1' }

  console.log(header('API'))
  console.log(`  Port : ${api.port}`)
  console.log(`  Host : ${api.host} ${dim('(localhost only)')}`)
  console.log('')

  const newPort = await input({
    message: 'API port:',
    default: String(api.port),
    validate: (v) => {
      const n = Number(v.trim())
      if (!Number.isInteger(n) || n < 1 || n > 65535) return 'Must be a valid port (1-65535)'
      return true
    },
  })

  updates.api = { port: Number(newPort.trim()) }
  console.log(ok(`API port set to ${newPort.trim()}`))
}

}

import { nanoid } from 'nanoid'
import type { AgentInstance } from './agent-instance.js'
import type { ChannelAdapter } from './channel.js'
import type { SessionStatus } from './types.js'
import { createChildLogger, createSessionLogger, type Logger } from './log.js'
const moduleLog = createChildLogger({ module: 'session' })

export class Session {
  id: string
  channelId: string
  threadId: string = ''
  agentName: string
  workingDirectory: string
  agentInstance: AgentInstance
  status: SessionStatus = 'initializing'
  name?: string
  promptQueue: string[] = []
  promptRunning: boolean = false
  createdAt: Date = new Date()
  adapter?: ChannelAdapter  // Set by wireSessionEvents for renaming
  pendingPermission?: { requestId: string; resolve: (optionId: string) => void }
  log: Logger

  constructor(opts: {
    id?: string
    channelId: string
    agentName: string
    workingDirectory: string
    agentInstance: AgentInstance
  }) {
    this.id = opts.id || nanoid(12)
    this.channelId = opts.channelId
    this.agentName = opts.agentName
